issue.title: perf: mark lazy event handler factory as side-effect-free
issue.body:
Allow bundlers to remove unused `defineLazyEventHandler()` calls.

Repro bundle sizes with H3 `2.0.8` and Rolldown `1.2.14`:

| Fixture | Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unused lazy handler | Minified | 14,140 B | 1,214 B |
| Unused lazy handler | Gzip | 5,107 B | 714 B |

[Reproduction](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/h3-pure-lazy), Node `24.21.0` and pnpm `11.28.5`:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch repro/h3-pure-lazy https://github.com/onmax/repros.git h3-repro
cd h3-repro
node verify.mjs
```

comment.body: @NgoQuocViet2001 The supplied code confirms that `cancel()` sets `cancelled`, and `while (!cancelled)` prevents further `next()` calls after an in-flight skipped value completes. This addresses the cancellation finding for iterators without `return()`. I accept leaving out the macrotask yield. The unbounded skipped-value case can still starve the event loop, but adding scheduling behavior is not required for this fix. I retract that part of my recommendation. --- If you found this review helpful, would you consider giving us a shout-out on [X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?related=CodeRabbitAI&text=%40coderabbitai%20caught%20a%20cancellation%20bug%3A%20skipped%20iterator%20values%20could%20keep%20pulling%20after%20cancel().%20A%20cancellation%20flag%20and%20tests%20now%20stop%20it%20in%20web%20and%20Node.%20Try%20CodeRabbit%20for%20sharper%20reviews%20%F0%9F%90%87&url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fh3js%2Fh3%2Fpull%2F1615%23discussion_r4360035970)? Thank you for using CodeRabbit! ✅ Review thread resolved. You are interacting with an AI system.

The cancellation part was real: the loop kept calling `next()` after cancel as long as values were skipped and the iterator had no `return()` (generators already stop there). af78734 adds a `cancelled` flag that ends the loop, with a test that fails on the previous commit in both web and node.

I left out the macrotask yield. An iterator that keeps returning skipped values without awaiting anything would spin a `for await` loop the same way, and `iterable()` doesn't schedule timers anywhere else, so I'd rather not add one for this case.
